title: ¿Cuántas veces tendrías que doblar una hoja para llegar a la Luna? 🌕
staging_mode_proposal: world: the payoff is height: the stack climbs out of a landscape, past a mountain, through the sky into black space to the Moon; only a modelled world gives the camera something to climb past (reference objects, format policy 'Dynamism')
curiosity_reason: The 'you can't fold it more than seven times' challenge is a playground classic; enormous; testable on the spot.
hook_question: ¿Cuántas veces tendrías que doblar una hoja de papel para llegar a la Luna?
false_belief: Harían falta miles o millones de dobleces.
turn: Scene 7: on paper it takes 42 folds, but in real life nobody has passed 12 (Britney Gallivan, 2002, with a strip more than a kilometre long).
closing_reframe: No hacen falta millones de dobleces: cada uno duplica todo lo anterior.
share_archetype: ese amigo que, cuando le cuentas esto, saca una hoja para intentarlo
engine_reason: code3d on the asset route (CLAUDE.md engine selection: rigid objects, figures and energy graphics on a stylised stage); sealed library assets and poses where named, geometric builds otherwise.
description:
¿Cuántas veces tendrías que doblar una hoja para llegar a la Luna? Solo 42, porque cada doblez duplica el grosor.
Pero en la vida real, nadie ha pasado de 12. 🌕
Envíaselo a ese amigo que, cuando le cuentas esto, saca una hoja para intentarlo.
wardrobe: Scene 3 (a generic person, the viewer's stand-in): default outfit (skin #D99E7A, shirt #2973CC blue, pants #2E3347 grey, boots #59331A): a lone figure keeps the recurring character.
Scene 7 (the student, clearly a different person): fig_skin #C68A62, fig_shirt #D9483B red, fig_pants #3A3F5C navy, fig_boots #EDEDED white.

scenes.name: hook
scenes.narration: ¿Cuántas veces tendrías que doblar una hoja de papel para llegar a la Luna? Seguro piensas que miles. Son muchísimas menos.
scenes.what_changes: A single white sheet lies on flat ground at dusk with the Moon low on the horizon; tag ¿MILES? appears; the sheet folds in half once.
scenes.transformation: hoja extendida en el suelo → se dobla por primera vez
scenes.camera: empuje bajo desde la Luna en el horizonte hasta la hoja

elements.name: sheet of paper
elements.route: build, geometric (thin white slab with a soft fold)

scenes.name: duplica
scenes.narration: Una hoja mide una décima de milímetro. Cada vez que la doblas, su grosor se duplica: dos hojas, cuatro, ocho.
scenes.what_changes: Macro on the edge of the stack: one layer becomes two, four, eight as each fold lands; a counter doubles in step.
scenes.transformation: una capa → dos → cuatro → ocho capas
scenes.camera: primer plano lateral del canto que sube con cada doblez

scenes.name: persona
scenes.narration: Al doblez catorce, la pila ya es más alta que una persona.
scenes.what_changes: Pull-back: the stack shoots up to 1.6 m and stands beside a person, who looks up at it.
scenes.transformation: pila pequeña → pila más alta que una persona
scenes.camera: retroceso a plano medio junto a la persona

elements.name: person standing beside a stack of paper
elements.route: library human-figure, sealed pose standing (lone figure: default outfit)

scenes.name: montana
scenes.narration: Al doblez veintisiete, pasa la cima del Everest, la montaña más alta del mundo.
scenes.what_changes: The stack keeps growing; the camera climbs alongside it past a snow-capped mountain until the column rises above the summit and the clouds.
scenes.transformation: pila a ras de suelo → la pila supera la cima nevada
scenes.camera: subida vertical pegada a la pila, la montaña pasa de lado

elements.name: snow-capped mountain
elements.route: library terrain (BlenderKit RF mountain terrains, 400-700 MB; judged heavy) or a stylised build: rock peak with a snow cap material
elements.risk: medium: a stylised peak is iconic but organic; context = clouds and the stack beside it

scenes.name: espacio
scenes.narration: Al doblez treinta y dos, ya está en el espacio, más arriba de donde orbitan los astronautas.
scenes.what_changes: The sky darkens from blue to black and stars appear while the column keeps climbing; the curve of the horizon falls away below.
scenes.transformation: cielo azul → cielo negro con estrellas mientras la pila sigue subiendo
scenes.camera: retroceso lateral amplio que muestra la columna entera atravesando el cielo hasta el negro

elements.name: paper column rising into space
elements.route: stack build + world sky gradient and star field (shader)
elements.risk: medium: the column must still read as paper; its layered edge stays in frame

scenes.name: luna
scenes.narration: Y al doblez cuarenta y dos, supera los trescientos ochenta mil kilómetros: llega a la Luna.
scenes.what_changes: The Moon grows in frame as the column's tip reaches it and passes its distance; the camera swings around the Moon to look back down the thin column.
scenes.transformation: Luna lejana → la punta de la pila llega a la Luna
scenes.camera: órbita alrededor de la Luna mirando hacia la pila

elements.name: the Moon
elements.route: library BlenderKit 'Moon' by Cyberking 42 (4611d12e, CC0, 50.7 MB; thumbnail not viewable from search, judge at the asset step) or a build: grey sphere with a crater material
elements.risk: low-medium: a grey cratered sphere in black space is iconic

scenes.name: giro
scenes.narration: Pero en la vida real, nadie ha pasado de doce. En 2002, una estudiante lo logró con una tira de papel de más de un kilómetro.
scenes.what_changes: The turn: the column collapses back to the ground; a very long paper strip runs to the horizon and a student, at its end, finishes the twelfth fold of a small thick wad.
scenes.transformation: columna hasta la Luna → se desploma y queda una tira larguísima doblada doce veces
scenes.camera: travelling largo a lo largo de la tira hasta la estudiante

elements.name: person beside a long strip of folded paper
elements.route: library human-figure, sealed pose standing (a different person: distinct wardrobe); strip geometric
elements.risk: low-medium: the strip must read as paper; the wad is the cue

scenes.name: cierre
scenes.narration: Así que no hacen falta millones de dobleces: cada uno duplica todo lo anterior. Envíaselo a ese amigo que, cuando le cuentas esto, saca una hoja para intentarlo.
scenes.what_changes: Single reframe image: one sheet folds once more and the doubling replays as a quick climb from the ground to the Moon in one continuous move.
scenes.transformation: una hoja → un doblez más y la pila vuelve a subir hasta la Luna
scenes.camera: subida continua de la hoja a la Luna

sources: Paper thickness about 0.1 mm for ordinary office paper (80 g/m2). FLAGGED: cite a paper-standard or manufacturer spec at the beat sheet; the arithmetic below holds for 0.1 mm.
Arithmetic: 0.1 mm x 2^14 = 1.64 m (taller than a person); 2^26 = 6.7 km < Everest, 2^27 = 13.4 km > Everest; 2^32 = 429.5 km; 2^41 = 219,902 km < Moon, 2^42 = 439,805 km > Moon.
Everest 8,848.86 m (joint China-Nepal survey, 2020). FLAGGED to cite at the beat sheet (widely published).
International Space Station orbit about 400-420 km (NASA). FLAGGED to cite at the beat sheet; 2^32 = 430 km clears it.
Mean Earth-Moon distance 384,400 km (NASA). FLAGGED to cite at the beat sheet; 'supera los trescientos ochenta mil kilómetros' holds.

Record: Britney Gallivan (USA), a high-school student, folded a single piece of paper in half 12 times, using tissue paper 4,000 ft (1,219 m) long; Guinness World Records 'Most times to fold a piece of paper' (record dated 27 January 2002) and GWR news, 22 October 2025 (live search 2026-11-11). The narration says 'una tira de papel de más de un kilómetro' and does not name the paper type.
simplifications: Folding is idealised: real paper cannot be folded past about a dozen times, which is the turn.
The column is drawn as a thin straight tower; it would really be a wad as wide as the last fold allows.
